# Constructive data modeling

> A source-backed Foldkit study deck after Alexis King's Software Should Work 2026 talk.

The deck has ten stable slides selected with `?slide=<slide-id>`. Keyboard controls are Left, Right, Space, Home, and End. Browser, command-line, and terminal hosts consume the same renderer-neutral Program, Model, and Message union.

## Primary sources

- [Conference recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0BXuYlNrUmE)
- [Authored slide source](https://github.com/lexi-lambda/talks/tree/c43b8f2d7645c78fb60c2e724f47f8b0c4872277/2026-07%20constructive%20data%20modeling)
- [Software Should Work 2026](https://softwareshould.work/)
- [Parse, don't validate](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/blog/2019/11/05/parse-don-t-validate/)
- [Alexis King](https://lexi-lambda.github.io/)
